title: Enough Capacity, Not Enough Redundancy
description: One server easily handles 500 RPS and a 40 GB working set, but the service must survive a machine failure. Why run several app instances?

options.text: To improve availability even though one machine has enough capacity.
options.explanation: Capacity and failure tolerance are separate requirements. Multiple instances behind redundant routing avoid making one app machine the whole service.

options.text: Because vertical scaling never supports a 40 GB working set.
options.explanation: Modern instances can hold far more memory; the stated problem is redundancy.

options.text: Because each extra app instance automatically shards the database.
options.explanation: Scaling the stateless tier does not distribute database ownership or writes.

options.text: Because adding CPU to one machine creates an independent failure domain.
options.explanation: A larger machine is still one machine and can fail as a unit.
